title: Local cocartesian edges agree with global lifts when transport exists
statement: Use small quasicategories, equivalence edges and simplicial pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner fibrations and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to C$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories. For an edge $a:c\to d$ in $C$ put $E_a=E\times_{C,a}\Delta^1$, and call an edge $u:x\to y$ over $a$ locally cocartesian when $(u,\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1})$ is cocartesian for $E_a\to\Delta^1$. If a global $p$-cocartesian lift of $a$ exists with source $x$, then $u$ is locally cocartesian if and only if it is $p$-cocartesian. For a degenerate base edge $a=\mathrm{id}_c$, these equivalent conditions are also equivalent to $u$ being an equivalence in the vertex fibre $E_c=E\times_C\{c\}$. Consequently, for a fully scaled categorical pattern $\mathfrak P=(C,S,\{p_\alpha\})$ and a $\mathfrak P$-fibered marked object $(E,T)\to(C,S)$ of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], $T$ consists exactly of the locally cocartesian edges over $S$, and its edges over $\mathrm{id}_c$ are exactly the equivalences of $E_c$.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Lemma B.2.4(a), printed pp.1483-1484: comparison of local and global cocartesian edges for the fully scaled pattern convention of the DAG. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical fact.

proof.text: Put $r:E_a\to\Delta^1$ and $j:E_a\to E$. The pullback is degreewise, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Every inner-horn lifting problem for $r$ projects to one for $p$; combine its filler in $E$ with the prescribed simplex in $\Delta^1$ to obtain the filler in $E_a$. Thus $r$ is inner. Since $\Delta^1$ is a quasicategory, filling its inner horn first and then lifting shows that $E_a$ is a quasicategory. The same argument over a constant base simplex makes every strict fibre $E_c$ a quasicategory. If $v$ is $p$-cocartesian, any outer-horn problem for $(v,\mathrm{id})$ projects to a problem with first edge $v$ in $E$. Its $p$-cocartesian filler, paired with the prescribed simplex of $\Delta^1$, fills the original problem. This proves global implies local, directly from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], without assuming lifts from other sources.

source.place: Definition 2.4.1.11 and Remark 2.4.1.12, opposite dual; degreewise horn calculation.

proof.text: We will use the following immediate consequence of [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift]. An equivalence edge in the total quasicategory of any inner fibration is cocartesian for that fibration: apply its first-outer-horn clause in every dimension $n\geq2$, exactly the predicate of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. In particular an equivalence of $E_d$ is $p$-cocartesian after inclusion into $E$, because its inverse and its two inverse triangles remain inverse witnesses under the simplicial inclusion, using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.5, opposite dual; equivalence outer-horn criterion.

proof.text: Suppose $u:x\to y$ is locally cocartesian, and choose the hypothesized global lift $v:x\to z$ of $a$. In $E_a$ both $\widetilde v$ and $\widetilde u$ are $r$-cocartesian (Step 1). Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] to the inner fibration $r$ and base edge $01$. Both are initial in its lift quasicategory $L((x,0),01)$. Its comparison clause supplies an edge between these initial lifts, with target comparison $h:(z,1)\to(y,1)$ an equivalence in the strict fibre $r^{-1}(1)=E_d$, and with its commuting $2$-simplex. Projecting to $E$ gives the triangle with edges $v,h,u$, lying over the simplex $s_1a$ (vertices $c,d,d$). The strict fibre identification here is degreewise: a simplex over the constant vertex $1$ is precisely an $E$-simplex over the constant vertex $d$. Thus the comparison and its inverse witnesses really lie in $E_d$.

source.place: Remark 2.4.1.9 and Remark 2.4.2.13, opposite duals; uniqueness of the locally cocartesian lift.

proof.text: The comparison $h$ from Step 3 is $p$-cocartesian by Step 2. In the triangle $(v,h,u)$ its first edge $v$ is $p$-cocartesian by hypothesis. The cancellation/composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] therefore says that $h$ is $p$-cocartesian if and only if $u$ is. This proves local implies global, completing the first equivalence. Only the one lift $v$ with the prescribed source was used.

Now let $a=\mathrm{id}_c$. The degenerate lift $1_x$ is globally cocartesian by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], so the first equivalence applies without any further existence assumption. If $u$ is globally cocartesian, apply the initial-lift comparison of that node to $1_x$ and $u$ in $L(x,\mathrm{id}_c)$ for $p$ itself. It yields an equivalence $h:x\to y$ in $E_c$ and a triangle $(1_x,h,u)$ over the constant $2$-simplex at $c$. All of this triangle lies in $E_c$. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], its classes in $h(E_c)$ satisfy $[u]=[h][1_x]=[h]$. The class $[h]$ is invertible, hence the same node's characterization of invertible classes proves that $u$ is an equivalence in $E_c$. Conversely a fibre equivalence is globally cocartesian by Step 2 and locally cocartesian by Step 1. This proves all three equivalent conditions with the equivalence in the strict fibre, rather than just in $E$.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.1.6, Remark 2.4.1.9 and Proposition 2.4.1.5, opposite duals; fibrewise comparison.

proof.text: Finally condition (i) of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy] makes $p$ inner; its total space is a quasicategory by the same horn argument as Step 1 since $C$ is a quasicategory. Condition (ii) gives a global cocartesian lift for every source over every $a\in S$, and identifies $T$ with precisely the global cocartesian edges over $S$. Apply Steps 1--4 separately to each such source and edge to replace global by local in this description of $T$. Every degenerate edge belongs to $S$, so Step 5 identifies its marked lifts with precisely the equivalences in $E_c$. No use of the cone conditions (iii)--(iv), nonempty fibres, or additional base edges is required.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Lemma B.2.4(a), printed pp.1483--1484, under the fully scaled pattern convention of the DAG.

lean.statement: theorem cocartesian_local_global : (∀ {E C : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory E] [Quasicategory C] (p : E ⟶ C) (_h_inner : InnerFibration p) (u : E _⦋1⦌), (∃ v : E _⦋1⦌, E.δ 1 v = E.δ 1 u ∧ p.app _ v = p.app _ u ∧ IsCocartesianEdge p (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm v)) → (IsLocallyOperadicCocartesian p (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm u) ↔ IsCocartesianEdge p (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm u))) ∧ (∀ {E C : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory E] [Quasicategory C] (p : E ⟶ C) (_h_inner : InnerFibration p) (c : C _⦋0⦌) (u : (fiber p c) _⦋1⦌), (IsLocallyOperadicCocartesian p (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm u ≫ pullback.snd (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) c) p) ↔ IsEquivalenceEdge (fiber p c) u) ∧ (IsCocartesianEdge p (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm u ≫ pullback.snd (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) c) p) ↔ IsEquivalenceEdge (fiber p c) u)) ∧ (∀ (P : CategoricalPattern.{u}) (X : CategoricalPattern.Object P), IsCategoricalPatternFibered P X → (∀ e : X.underlying.underlying _⦋1⦌, e ∈ X.underlying.marking ↔ IsLocallyOperadicCocartesian X.map (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm e) ∧ X.map.app _ e ∈ P.marked) ∧ (∀ (c : P.carrier _⦋0⦌) (e : (fiber X.map c) _⦋1⦌), (pullback.snd (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) c) X.map).app _ e ∈ X.underlying.marking ↔ IsEquivalenceEdge (fiber X.map c) e))
